sources.citation: Philip JH. Gas Man(R) Workbook and Laboratory Manual. Chestnut Hill, MA: Med Man Simulations, Inc.; document dated 2012-05-16, preface dated October 2010. Appendix B, 'The Gas Man Approach', Model Parameters table (Table A-1), page 168.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation (see docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy'). READ AT THE SOURCE 2026-09-06, from a copy of the front matter and appendices supplied by the project owner; this repository does not hold it, because it is publisher-copyright material and the repository is public. That route is neither of the two .claude/rules/citing-sources.md describes, and PL-XJ5P carries the gap. Page 168's Model Parameters table gives, under Volume / Flow / Rel. Flow: Circuit 8.0; Alveoli 2.5; Blood 5.00; VRG 6.0, 3.80, 0.76; Muscle 33.0, 0.90, 0.18; Fat 14.5, 0.30, 0.06. SO THE TABLE SUPPLIES SEVEN OF THE ELEVEN STORED VALUES AND NOT ALL ELEVEN, which is what this note claimed before it was read. Verified present and exactly equal: alveolar_gas_volume_l 2.5, tissue_groups.vessel_rich.volume_l 6.0 and perfusion_fraction 0.76, tissue_groups.muscle.volume_l 33.0 and perfusion_fraction 0.18, tissue_groups.fat.volume_l 14.5 and perfusion_fraction 0.06. default_cardiac_output_l_min 5.0 is present only as the sum of the Flow column (3.80 + 0.90 + 0.30 = 5.00 L/min), not as a row of its own. THREE STORED VALUES ARE NOT IN THIS TABLE AT ALL. venous_pool_volume_l has no counterpart at any value: the table's Blood row reads 5.00 L, which is a blood volume rather than this model's venous mixing pool. The value stored here was 1.0 L until 2026-09-07 and is now 1.222 L from Davis and Mapleson, whose entry is below; neither figure is in this table. PL-3YZW carries what that cost and how it was answered. weight_kg 70.0 and default_alveolar_ventilation_l_min 4.0 are program defaults set through the interface, described qualitatively at page 183 ('Patient default options include:', Appendix E) without numbers; the chapters supplied state no numeric default for either. The citation before this one named that page-183 section, which describes the controls and carries none of the values. NO PRIMARY SOURCE HAS BEEN ADOPTED FOR ANY OF THE ELEVEN PARAMETERS. Five carry a measurement cited alongside and explicitly not adopted, in the entries below - alveolar_gas_volume_l, default_cardiac_output_l_min, tissue_groups.muscle.volume_l, tissue_groups.muscle.perfusion_fraction and tissue_groups.fat.perfusion_fraction. Of the rest, weight_kg is a labelling convention rather than a measurement (no equation reads it; see docs/MODEL.md); venous_pool_volume_l is a well-stirred mixing volume whose only role is the mixed-venous time constant V_v/Q, here 14.7 s, and is NOT the physiologic venous blood volume - it is the one value in this file that now carries a source other than the Workbook; default_alveolar_ventilation_l_min is a derived convention; and tissue_groups.vessel_rich.volume_l, tissue_groups.vessel_rich.perfusion_fraction and tissue_groups.fat.volume_l are lumped-compartment aggregates for which no single measurement exists - the vessel-rich group implies 3.8 L/min into 6 L, about 63 mL per 100 mL of tissue per minute, which is the right order for a lumped brain/heart/liver/kidney/viscera compartment but is not a measured figure. THE UPSTREAM THE WORKBOOK NAMES FOR THOSE SEVEN VALUES, NOW READ. The note printed beneath the same table reads, in these words: 'Values for volume, flow and relative flow are taken from Lowe and Ernst, 1981'. Its reference 23 is 'Lowe, HF and Ernst, EA. The Quantitative Practice of Anesthesia: Use of Closed Circuit. Baltimore: Williams & Wilkins, 1981' - printed with the initial HF there and as HJ at references 22 and 24, so that bibliography is internally inconsistent. THE BOOK HAS SINCE BEEN OPENED AND CARRIES ITS OWN SOURCES ENTRY, IMMEDIATELY BELOW. It deliberately had none until 2026-09-08, because giving an unread document its own citation line is the failure the Mapleson entries were removed from this file for. What this entry establishes remains only what the Workbook says about where its own numbers came from, read at the source. It is also a different lineage from the one this file assumed until 2026-09-06 - Mapleson's papers, named here on the strength of their titles; the Workbook attributes nothing to Mapleson. PL-7HDS carried reading Lowe and Ernst, the link that decides whether this chain ends in a measurement or in another compilation - and it ends in neither, the book collecting the figures and citing them onward again. READ AT THE SOURCE 2026-09-08 (PL-7HDS), AFTER TWO ROUNDS AT ONE REMOVE. Two peer-reviewed papers that used the book were supplied by the project owner on 2026-09-06 and read at full-text depth - Lerou and Booij, and Couto da Silva, Mapleson and Vickers, whose entries are below - and the book itself was then reached on 2026-09-08 through an interlibrary loan. Its entry follows this one and carries the reading; what remains here is only what the Workbook says. THE INITIAL IS HJ: both papers cite 'Lowe HJ, Ernst EA', PubMed indexes this author as 'Lowe H J' on every closed-circuit paper from 1968 to 1994 (for example PMID 4271708, Anaesthesia 1974;29(1):110-1), and the interlibrary-loan record for the scan prints the author as 'Lowe, Harry J.', so the Workbook's reference-23 'HF' is a misprint. WHAT THE SOURCE READING DID TO THIS ENTRY'S CLAIM. 'Values for volume, flow and relative flow are taken from Lowe and Ernst, 1981' now has the book behind it rather than a report of the book, and it holds for three of the seven values and not for four. The three are alveolar volume's absence from the book (so the Workbook cannot have taken it from there), the vessel-rich volume and the vessel-rich flow fraction; the four are the muscle and fat volumes and flow fractions, which no grouping of the book's ten compartments reproduces. The next entry carries the figures, the arithmetic and what it does and does not convict anybody of. IT ALSO SETTLES THE TIER, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE CHAIN DOES NOT END THERE. The book cites its own volumes and flows onward to four references it does not reproduce in the supplied pages, so it is tier 2 rather than tier 1 and the Workbook's upstream has an upstream. All seven values stay tier 3 and unadopted, unchanged by any of this: reading where Gas Man's numbers came from is not evidence that they were measured.

sources.citation: Lowe HJ, Ernst EA. The Quantitative Practice of Anesthesia: Use of Closed Circuit. Baltimore: Williams & Wilkins; 1981. Chapter 4, 'Uptake and Distribution', pages 55-60, with figure 4.1 on page 57; chapter 5, pages 82-84, with table 5.6 on page 83. ISBN 0683052004 (9780683052008); OCLC 6665746.
sources.note: Tier 2, secondary synthesis, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED. This is the upstream the Gas Man Workbook names for its volume and flow values, and the entry above is where that attribution is recorded. READ AT THE SOURCE 2026-09-08 (PL-7HDS). Pages 55-60 and 82-84 were supplied by the project owner as an interlibrary-loan scan (RapidILL; lender University of Sydney Main Library, borrower University of Wisconsin-Madison Memorial Library, processed 2026-09-07), the pages having been narrowed to 57 and 83 by the two second-hand readings below. This repository does not hold the file, because it is publisher-copyright material and the repository is public; the scan carries its own Australian Copyright Act notice. That route is a third one, neither of the two .claude/rules/citing-sources.md describes and not the personal-access route the Workbook came by, and PL-XJ5P carries the gap. THE PAGES OUTSIDE THAT RANGE WERE NOT SUPPLIED AND ARE NOT READ - among them chapter 4's reference list, which is why the four references below are identified only as far as the chapter's own narrative names them. THE MODEL PATIENT IS 100 KG, NOT 70. Figure 4.1b and every chapter-5 table are tabulated for a 100-kg patient, and page 56 says why in these words: 'Because the patient weighs 100 kg, the organ weights can also be read as per cent of total body weight.' THAT IS WHY THE MATERIAL REACHES THIS PROJECT AS FRACTIONS: Lerou and Booij's Table 6 of volume fractions of body mass and flow fractions of cardiac output is this table divided by 100, not a normalization they performed. Nothing in the book states a 70-kg parameter set, so every figure below is a per-cent read off a 100-kg table and then applied at 70 kg, which is this project's arithmetic and not the book's. THE BOOK CITES THESE VALUES ONWARD; IT MEASURES NOTHING HERE. Page 56, in these words: 'The figure models a 100-kg patient with normal physiologic organ volumes and blood flows (9, 19, 20, 26).' Chapter 4's narrative on page 55 names references 9, 19 and 20 as Mapleson, Smith et al. and Zwart et al. - all three cited there as authors of compartmental or multiple-model uptake models - and does not name 26 anywhere in the supplied pages. SO THE TIER IS 2 AND CANNOT BECOME 1: a monograph collecting other people's figures, per docs/MODEL.md 'Source hierarchy'. The chain the Workbook opens does not end in a measurement here. It ends one link further on, at four references nobody on this project has read, and PL-8SDL carries identifying them. WHAT FIGURE 4.1b PRINTS, page 57, columns a to d, read off the page image rather than off the scan's text layer, which mangles the figure. Organ, per cent of cardiac output, weight in kg, blood flow in L/min: Lung (100), 0.8, (6.3); Kidney 25, 0.4, 1.6; Heart 5, 0.4, 0.3; Brain 16, 2.1, 1.0; Liver 30, 5.7, 1.9; Muscle 13, 42.6, 0.8; Skin 3, 10.0, 0.2; Bone 2, 12.0, 0.15; Connective tissue 1, 4.0, 0.05; Adipose 5, 15.0, 0.3; Blood -, 7.0, -; Total 100, 100.0, 6.3. The ten tissue weights sum to 93.0 and blood is 7.0, which are Lerou and Booij's 0.930 and 0.07 M. CARDIAC OUTPUT IS ALLOMETRIC, AND THAT IS NOW READ AT THE SOURCE. Page 59 gives the cardiac output for its worked prime dose as 2 kg^(3/4), 'or 63.25 dl', for the 100-kg patient - the symbol printed as Q with an overdot - which is 0.2 x M^(3/4) in L/min, giving 6.32 L/min at the book's 100 kg and 4.84 L/min at 70 kg. The book's own worked 63.25 dl is what confirms the exponent independently of reading a superscript off a scan, and two further figures inside the book agree with it: figure 4.1b's flow column totals 6.3 L/min, and table 5.6's Blood row of 1,891 ml is CA x lambda_B/G x Q at CA = 65 ml/dl, lambda_B/G = 0.46 and Q = 63.25 dl/min. This is the relation da Silva, Mapleson and Vickers report second-hand, and their report was right. The stored default_cardiac_output_l_min of 5.0 does not reconcile with it at 70 kg; 5.00 L/min needs 73.1 kg. PL-YKSM carries that discrepancy and the decision it poses. HOW THE BOOK RECONCILES WITH WHAT THIS FILE STORES, at M = 70 kg. THE VESSEL-RICH PAIR REPRODUCES EXACTLY AND UNIQUELY. Kidney plus heart plus brain plus liver is 8.6 per cent of body weight, 6.02 L at 70 kg against the stored 6.0, at 25 + 5 + 16 + 30 = 76 per cent of cardiac output against the stored 0.76. Searching all 1,023 non-empty groupings of the ten compartments at a tolerance of 0.5 percentage points, that grouping is the ONLY one matching both the stored volume and the stored flow fraction. THE MUSCLE AND FAT FIGURES REPRODUCE UNDER NO GROUPING AT ALL: the same exhaustive search returns zero groupings matching both for muscle (stored 33.0 L at 0.18, against the book's muscle row at 29.8 L and 0.13) and zero for fat (stored 14.5 L at 0.06, against adipose at 10.5 L and 0.05). WHAT DOES SURVIVE FOR THOSE FOUR IS THE SPLIT, NOT THE VALUES. The book's five non-vessel-rich compartments - muscle, skin, bone, connective tissue and adipose - take 13 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 5 = 24 per cent of cardiac output, and the stored muscle and fat fractions sum to 0.18 + 0.06 = 0.24. Their volumes do not follow: 83.6 per cent of body weight is 58.5 L at 70 kg against the stored 33.0 + 14.5 = 47.5 L, 11.0 L less. So Gas Man appears to have kept the book's 76/24 flow split and redistributed the 24 across two compartments where the book has five, over a smaller total tissue volume. THAT IS THIS PROJECT'S ARITHMETIC AND IT CONVICTS NOBODY: Gas Man may lump differently, or work from a page outside this range, and the book prints more than one table. THE EIGHT-COMPARTMENT TABLE LEROU AND BOOIJ REPORT IS THE BOOK'S OWN LUMPING, AND THEIR REPORT IS FAITHFUL. Table 5.6, page 83, prints Lung 0.8, Kidney 0.4, Heart 0.4, Brain 2.1, Liver 5.7, Muscle 42.6, Connective tissue 26, Adipose 15 litres, with Blood 7 and Circuit 10 - the connective-tissue row being figure 4.1b's Skin 10.0 plus Bone 12.0 plus Connective tissue 4.0, and its 0.4 L/min flow being 0.2 plus 0.15 plus 0.05. Checking a second-hand report against the document is the thing this entry can do that the previous readings could not, and it holds in every figure. ALVEOLAR GAS VOLUME IS NOT IN THE BOOK AS A QUANTITY OF ITS OWN. Page 58 states that the ventilatory volume Vvent is the circuit volume plus the patient's functional residual capacity and that 'During anesthesia for most adults Vvent is about 100 dl'; table 5.6 carries that 10 L as a single Circuit row and prints no alveolar gas volume. The book therefore supplies no upstream for alveolar_gas_volume_l = 2.5 L, which is a stronger statement than the earlier 'untouched': the quantity is not merely absent from the pages read, it is lumped away at the point the book defines it. Gas Man's Circuit 8.0 plus Alveoli 2.5 is 10.5 L against that 10 L, which is this project's arithmetic against a lumped figure and is a source for neither half. ONE STATEMENT BEARS ON FAT PERFUSION AND DISAGREES WITH WHAT IS STORED. Page 56, in these words: 'the perfusion of adipose tissues equals that of muscle and skin (0.02 L/minute/kg) under basal conditions.' The stored fractions do not have them equal - 0.18 x 5.0 / 33.0 = 0.027 L/min/kg for muscle against 0.06 x 5.0 / 14.5 = 0.021 for fat, a ratio of 0.76 where the book has 1.0. That is the same direction as the Frayn and Karpe entry below, which reports fasting adipose blood flow per 100 g as similar to resting skeletal muscle, and it is a second reachable statement of the ratio the Heinonen entry could not settle. It is not a candidate for adoption: the book measures nothing, and this is its basal-conditions modelling assumption. PAGE 83 ALSO CARRIES PARTITION COEFFICIENTS, which is what Lerou and Booij's Table 5 cites it for. Table 5.6's tissue/blood column for nitrous oxide reads Lung 1.0, Kidney 0.87, Heart 1.13, Brain 1.06, Liver 0.93, Muscle 0.86, Connective tissue 0.8, Adipose 3, at lambda_B/G 0.46 and MAC 101. This model carries no nitrous oxide and no isoflurane coefficient appears in the supplied pages, so none of it is a candidate for any stored value; it is recorded because the page was cited, reached and read. NOTHING IS PROMOTED OR ADOPTED BY ANY OF THIS, and the reason is worth stating rather than leaving to the tier. A tier-2 document may be adopted on a recorded decision, the way Davis and Mapleson was for the venous pool - but for the four values that do not reproduce there is nothing here to adopt, and for the two that do, adopting would mean naming as the authority a compilation whose own four sources are unread. What the reading buys is that the Workbook's attribution has been checked against the document rather than against a report of it, and that the tier of the next link is now known to be a question rather than an assumption.

sources.citation: Meybohm P, et al. Context-sensitive decrement times for inhaled anesthetics in obese patients explored with Gas Man. Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing. 2021;35:897-908.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation. Meybohm et al. is a Gas Man simulation study; its description of the standard 70 kg model is a description of that product's parameter set, not an independent measurement of it. Citing it alongside the Workbook adds a journal name to the same tier-3 provenance rather than a second, independent source. READ AT FULL TEXT 2026-09-07 from PubMed Central (PMC7943506), which is the second of the two citations this file carried for the venous pool when the value was first written (the key was named venous_blood_volume_l until 2026-09-07). IT STATES NO VENOUS VOLUME. Its body text describes Gas Man as 'a flow-limited four-compartment mammillary model (alveolar gas, the vessel-rich group, muscle group and fat group)' - a list with no blood or venous compartment in it at all - and gives no compartment volume in litres anywhere in its prose. Its Tables 1-3 could not be retrieved: the PubMed full-text service returns the article body without table contents, and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov is refused by the egress proxy, so this entry cannot exclude a parameter listing in a table. PL-XJ5P carries that route gap.

sources.citation: Hudgel DW, Devadatta P. Decrease in functional residual capacity during sleep in normal humans. Journal of Applied Physiology. 1984;57(5):1319-1322.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED, and the comparison for alveolar_gas_volume_l. Functional residual capacity by closed-circuit helium dilution in 10 healthy males: 3.14 +/- 0.01 L (mean +/- SE) awake, falling to 2.95 L in stage 2 sleep and 2.83 L in REM. FRC is the closest measured analogue of this model's lung gas volume. Taken with Wahba's approximately 20 percent reduction under general anaesthesia (next entry), 3.14 L x 0.80 = 2.51 L, so the stored 2.5 L sits within 0.5 percent of the awake measurement reduced by the anaesthetic effect. THAT RECONCILIATION IS THIS PROJECT'S ARITHMETIC, NOT A FINDING OF EITHER PAPER, and neither paper studied an anaesthetised subject at 70 kg. Posture during the awake measurement is not stated in the abstract. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 6520027) and read at abstract depth only 2026-09-06.

sources.citation: Wahba RW. Perioperative functional residual capacity. Canadian Journal of Anaesthesia. 1991;38(3):384-400.
sources.note: Tier 2, secondary synthesis, cited but not adopted; the second half of the alveolar_gas_volume_l comparison above. A review of the perioperative FRC literature, reporting that during general anaesthesia FRC is reduced by approximately 20 percent, more in the obese and in COPD, most likely through loss of inspiratory muscle tone. A review measures nothing and docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy admits a tier-2 source as the authority for a stored value only on a recorded decision, and none has been taken for this parameter; it is here because the stored 2.5 L is only interpretable as an anaesthetised subject's lung gas volume, and this is the reachable statement of how far anaesthesia moves FRC. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 2036700) and read at abstract depth only 2026-09-06.

sources.citation: Cattermole GN, Leung PYM, Ho GYL, Lau PWS, Chan CPY, Chan SSW, Smith BE, Graham CA, Rainer TH. The normal ranges of cardiovascular parameters measured using the ultrasonic cardiac output monitor. Physiological Reports. 2017;5(6):e13195.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED, and the comparison for default_cardiac_output_l_min. Cross-sectional study of 2218 healthy subjects aged 0.5-89; in the 50.0-74.9 kg weight band (n=686), which is the band containing this file's 70 kg subject, cardiac output was 5.51 L/min median with a 2.5th-97.5th centile range of 3.00-9.35 L/min. The stored 5.0 L/min is 9.3 percent below that median and well inside the range. Reference conditions matter here and are the reason this is not adopted: healthy Hong Kong Chinese subjects, awake, supine, at rest, measured by transcutaneous continuous-wave Doppler (USCOM) rather than thermodilution, and the authors state explicitly that normal ranges are specific to the measurement method because different methods carry systematic bias. None of that describes an anaesthetised patient. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 28320891) and read at full-text depth, including Tables 2 and 3, 2026-09-06.

sources.citation: Janssen I, Heymsfield SB, Wang ZM, Ross R. Skeletal muscle mass and distribution in 468 men and women aged 18-88 yr. Journal of Applied Physiology. 2000;89(1):81-88.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED, and the comparison for tissue_groups.muscle.volume_l. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging in 468 men and women: men had 33.0 kg of skeletal muscle absolute and 38.4 percent relative to body mass (women 21.0 kg and 30.6 percent). THE NUMERIC MATCH TO THE STORED 33.0 IS A COINCIDENCE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS A SOURCE. Two things separate them. First, the units differ: this model's compartment is a volume in litres and Janssen reports a mass in kilograms. Second, and larger, 33.0 kg at 38.4 percent implies a mean body mass of about 86 kg for that cohort of men, not 70 kg; scaled to a 70 kg subject at the same fraction the measurement gives about 26.9 kg, which is 18.5 percent below the stored figure. The implied body mass is this project's arithmetic from two reported numbers, not a value the paper states. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 10904038) and read at abstract depth only 2026-09-06.

sources.citation: Heinonen I, Bucci M, Kemppainen J, Knuuti J, Nuutila P, Boushel R, Kalliokoski KK. Regulation of subcutaneous adipose tissue blood flow during exercise in humans. Journal of Applied Physiology. 2012;112(6):1059-1063.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED, and the comparison for tissue_groups.fat.perfusion_fraction. Positron emission tomography measurement of subcutaneous adipose tissue blood flow in the thigh of six healthy young women: 1.0 +/- 0.3 mL per 100 g per minute at rest, and about 1.0 +/- 0.5 adjacent to inactive muscle at every exercise intensity. The stored fraction implies 0.06 x 5 L/min = 300 mL/min into a 14.5 L compartment, about 2.1 mL per 100 mL of tissue per minute; the comparison crosses a volume-to-mass boundary, and at an adipose density near 0.9 kg/L the stored figure is about 2.3 mL per 100 g per minute. Either way the model perfuses fat at ROUGHLY TWICE this measurement, which shortens the fat compartment's time constant and so the slow tail of every washout curve the simulator draws. Not adopted, and the measurement does not settle the question on its own: this is one depot in one small cohort, whereas the model's fat group is whole-body adipose, and depot-to-depot differences are real (see the Frayn and Karpe entry). The implied perfusion is this project's arithmetic. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 22223450) and read at abstract depth only 2026-09-06.

sources.citation: Frayn KN, Karpe F. Regulation of human subcutaneous adipose tissue blood flow. International Journal of Obesity. 2014;38(8):1019-1026.
sources.note: Tier 2, secondary synthesis, cited but not adopted; the comparison for tissue_groups.muscle.perfusion_fraction, and the reason the fat gap above is a question about the absolute level rather than about the ratio. This review states that fasting adipose tissue blood flow per 100 g is similar to that of resting skeletal muscle, and that subcutaneous adipose represents about 85 percent of all body fat. The stored fractions are consistent with the first statement: 0.18 x 5 L/min = 900 mL/min into 33 L is about 2.7 mL per 100 mL per minute for muscle against about 2.1 for fat, a ratio near 0.8. So the model's muscle-to-fat perfusion ratio matches the reachable literature even though its absolute fat perfusion is about twice Heinonen's resting thigh measurement. A review measures nothing and cannot be the authority for a stored value; no reachable primary measurement of whole-body resting skeletal muscle perfusion was found. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 24166067) and read at abstract depth only 2026-09-06.

sources.citation: Lerou JGC, Booij LHDJ. Model-based administration of inhalation anaesthesia. 1. Developing a system model. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2001;86(1):12-28. Table 6 and its reference 49.
sources.note: Tier 2, secondary synthesis, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED, and the best reachable evidence about what Lowe and Ernst 1981 contains - which is a different thing from evidence about the stored values, and must not be read as the second. A published multiple-gas system model of the circle absorber and patient. Its Table 6 gives eight body-compartment volumes as fractions of body mass and blood flows as fractions of cardiac output, captioned 'Values are data given by Lowe and Ernst' and cited to page 57 of the book; its Table 5 cites the book again at page 83 for nitrous oxide and isoflurane partition coefficients. THE TABLE IS THEIRS REPORTING THE BOOK, NOT THE BOOK - and the book has since been opened, so what this entry establishes is now bounded on both sides. Their report is faithful: every figure in Table 6 is figure 4.1b's 100-kg table divided by 100, with their connective-tissue row being the book's own chapter-5 lumping of skin, bone and connective tissue. What it could never establish, and what only the book could answer, is that the book cites those fractions onward rather than measuring them. See the Lowe and Ernst entry above for the figures, for how they reconcile with what this file stores at 70 kg - vessel-rich yes and uniquely, muscle and fat under no grouping at all - and for why nothing is promoted by any of it. Two further points of contact, neither adopted. Their model patient is the same anaesthetized 40-year-old 70 kg man, whose alveolar space they DERIVE as FRC plus half a tidal volume, 2.623 L BTPS, rather than taking it from the book - so they supply no upstream for this file's alveolar_gas_volume_l of 2.5. And their earlier model ran at a cardiac output of 4.84 L/min for that patient, which is what Lowe and Ernst's 0.2 x M^(3/4) gives at 70 kg and is not the 5.0 stored here; PL-YKSM carries that. Supplied as a PDF by the project owner and read at full-text depth 2026-09-06, including Tables 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 and the reference list. This repository does not hold the file: it is publisher-copyright material and the repository is public.

sources.citation: Couto da Silva JM, Mapleson WW, Vickers MD. Quantitative study of Lowe's square-root-of-time method of closed-system anaesthesia. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 1997;79(1):103-112.
sources.note: Tier 1 for its own clinical measurements, CITED BUT NOT ADOPTED, and used here only for what it reports about Lowe and Ernst 1981. A double-blind randomized study of Lowe's intermittent-injection method in 60 patients across halothane, enflurane and isoflurane, which measured none of this file's parameters. Its reference 2 is the book, cited to pages 19, 67-97, 175-179 and 215, and it takes three things from it: the unit-dose equation, the ratios of vapour volume at 37 C to liquid volume (240, 210 and 206 for the three agents), and a cardiac output 'estimated from 0.2 x M^(3/4)' with M the body mass in kg. NONE OF THE THREE IS A TISSUE VOLUME OR A PERFUSION FRACTION, so this paper says nothing about the seven values the Workbook credits to the book. The cardiac-output relation gives 4.84 L/min at 70 kg, against the 5.0 stored here and the 5.00 the Workbook's flow column sums to; 5.00 would need 73.1 kg. That reading is checked rather than assumed, the equation glyphs in the PDF being mangled: the paper's printed unit doses for a 70 kg 40-year-old, 0.94, 1.86 and 1.00 ml, reproduce to 0.944, 1.856 and 1.001 ml from D = 2 x 1.3 x (MAC/100) x Q x lambda / r at Q = 4.84, using the MAC, blood:gas and vapour:liquid values the paper itself states. Reproducing all three from one Q is what establishes the reading. THE SOURCE READING OF 2026-09-08 CONFIRMED IT: page 59 of the book prints 'Q = 2 kg^(3/4) or 63.25 dl' for its 100-kg patient, so this paper's report of the relation was right and the reconstruction above was unnecessary rather than wrong. The arithmetic is this project's; PL-YKSM carries the discrepancy. Note also that this paper's own MAC and blood:gas figures come from Mapleson 1996 and Steward et al. 1973, NOT from the book. Supplied as a PDF by the project owner and read at full-text depth 2026-09-06. This repository does not hold the file: it is publisher-copyright material and the repository is public.

sources.citation: Davis NR, Mapleson WW. Structure and quantification of a physiological model of the distribution of injected agents and inhaled anaesthetics. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 1981;53(4):399-405. Page 400 for the inhaled-anaesthetic pool sizes; Table III and the Appendix, pages 402-404, for the derivation.
sources.note: Tier 2, published model quantification, ADOPTED - see below. READ AT THE SOURCE 2026-09-07, from a PDF supplied by the project owner; this repository does not hold the file, because it is publisher-copyright material and the repository is public - the same route the Gas Man Workbook came by, and the gap PL-XJ5P carries. ADOPTED 2026-09-07 ON THE PROJECT OWNER'S DECISION: venous_pool_volume_l = 1.222 L comes from this paper. It is the first value in this file to carry a source other than the Gas Man Workbook, and the first published counterpart this parameter has ever had. Their standard man is 70 kg, 30-39 yr, 1.85 m2 (Table I), with a total blood volume of 5189 ml and a cardiac output of 6480 ml/min (Table III). Page 400 states, in terms, that FOR MODELS OF INHALED ANAESTHETICS the two venous pools may be combined, 'in which case it would be marginally more accurate to make the arterial pool 799 ml (15.4% of the total blood volume) and the combined venous pool 1222 ml (23.6%)'. That combined pool is the same object as this model's V_v: one well-stirred venous pool carrying tissue return. The Appendix derives it from ICRP (1975) blood distribution - 25.9% or 1344 ml of the total is of arterial composition, of which 17.2% or 623 ml sits in the 3621 ml of local systemic pools, leaving 721 ml central arterial and 847 ml central venous in their exact scheme - so the pool volumes are DERIVED to reproduce circulation times, not measured, which is why this is tier 2 and not tier 1. WHAT IT REPLACED WAS 1.0 L, WHICH NO SOURCE EVER CONTAINED. That value entered the repository at v0.1.0 under a Workbook citation belonging to its neighbours (PL-3YZW records the commit and the section), so what was given up by adopting is not Gas Man comparability but an unsourced number. The change moves the mixed-venous time constant V_v/Q from 12.0 s to 14.7 s at the stored 5.0 L/min cardiac output, visible on the mixed-venous trace through the first minute of every simulation. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PUBLISHED COMPARISONS, 2026-09-07: the 30-minute F_A/F_I wash-in distances are unchanged to two decimal places (+0.16, +0.31, +0.79, +0.38 SD), the pool being long equilibrated by then; the 5-minute F_A/F_A0 elimination ratios move 0.11 to 0.13 published SD FURTHER FROM their cohort means (sevoflurane +3.67 to +3.79, isoflurane +4.02 to +4.15, desflurane +1.02 to +1.13), because a larger pool returns more agent - the same direction the module already attributes to this model's rebreathing circuit rather than to tissue return. IT ALSO ANSWERS THE ARTERIAL QUESTION, AGAINST THE ARTERIAL READING. The suspicion PL-8ZJQ recorded was that 1.0 L might be an arterial compartment under a venous name, on Lerou and Booij's arterial fraction of 0.2, which is 0.98 L at their 4.9 L total and within 2% of what is stored. Davis and Mapleson's own arterial pool for an inhaled-anaesthetic model is 799 ml, 15.4% rather than 20%, so that coincidence does not survive the primary source. Their venous pool is the closer structural match on every reading, and the time constants nearly agree: 1222/6480 = 11.3 s against this file's 1.0/5.0 = 12.0 s. That agreement is a property of the time constant rather than of the volume, and it is not evidence of a shared lineage - Gas Man is not documented as having taken anything from this paper.

Ten are the Gas Man default 70 kg patient - tier 3, reference implementation - and the Workbook entry above records which of those appear in that product's own parameter table and which are interface defaults it states no number for. The eleventh, venous_pool_volume_l, is Davis and Mapleson 1981, adopted 2026-09-07 on the project owner's decision (PL-8ZJQ) and tier 2 because their pool volumes are derived from ICRP 1975 blood distribution to reproduce circulation times rather than measured. Five parameters carry a primary measurement cited alongside and explicitly not adopted, each of those notes giving the measured value and the difference; six have no comparison, and each note says why rather than leaving the silence to be read as an oversight.
